thread.title: Donald Trump's Texas rally turns violent as MAGA faithful get physical with protestors: 'They're paid by enemies of our nation,' president says - NewsBreak
thread.title_full: Donald Trump's Texas rally turns violent as MAGA faithful get physical with protestors: 'They're paid by enemies of our nation,' president says - NewsBreak

author: Samyarup Chowdhury
title: Donald Trump's Texas rally turns violent as MAGA faithful get physical with protestors: 'They're paid by enemies of our nation,' president says - NewsBreak
text:
By Samyarup Chowdhury ,
31 minutes ago President Donald Trump's supporters got physical with protestors at his Texas rally. BY: X/ACYN President Donald Trump’s Texas rally turned chaotic on Wednesday, October 7, as repeated protests inside the Freeman Coliseum in San Antonio led to physical confrontations between demonstrators and Trump supporters. At least half a dozen protesters interrupted the president as he urged Texas voters to support Republican Senate candidate Ken Paxton, with some escorted away by police and one demonstrator reportedly assaulted while leaving the arena. Trump dismissed the protesters as being paid to heckle him, claiming without evidence that “they’re paid by enemies of our nation.”
Protesters repeatedly interrupt Donald Trump President Donald Trump was interrupted several times during his remarks. BY: X/ACYN Trump was interrupted several times during his remarks, and in turn, the crowd booed the protesters before police removed some of them from the venue. “You know, many of these protesters are paid. You know that, right?” Trump said. “They’re paid by enemies of our nation.”
At one point, the president briefly stepped away from the microphone after a protester appeared to move toward the stage. After the man was removed, Trump said, “He’s going back home to mom. … But what he doesn’t know is his mom voted for Trump.”
Donald Trump supporters clash with demonstrators President Donald Trump also told demonstrators to ‘get the hell out of here’ and mocked their appearances. BY: UNSPLASH Supporters waved cowboy hats and chanted “USA” as they drowned out some protesters. Trump also told demonstrators to “get the hell out of here” and mocked their appearances. “I love where they all have the same exact size, beautiful pink and purple and blue and all different colors. And they’re perfect, made by the same printer, very expensive signs,” he said.
At least one confrontation escalated beyond verbal exchanges and got physical, as an older Trump supporter assaulted a protester as the demonstrator attempted to leave the arena. Other encounters involved shoving, hair pulling and kicking as the crowd jeered.
Donald Trump revisits controversial Iran remarks The San Antonio rally also saw President Donald Trump repeat comments that had previously sparked widespread criticism. BY: X/ACYN The San Antonio rally also saw Trump repeat comments that had previously sparked widespread criticism. He appeared to suggest that Iran could destroy San Diego or Los Angeles, saying, “Let them hit San Diego. Let them hit Los Angeles. … You want to see some bad things happen? You want to see a country that would be in free fall? We’re not going to let that happen. We protect our cities. We protect our country.”
Trump appeared to argue that without the war in Iran, American cities would face danger. However, critics have said his earlier remarks invited Iran to “take out” U.S. cities or suggested American cities are fair collateral, claims the White House denied. “He was clearly stating U.S. cities would have been threatened if a nuclear Iran hadn’t been stopped,” White House communications director Steven Cheung said earlier this week.
Donald Trump’s endorsement of Ken Paxton Ken Paxton, whom Donald Trump endorsed after turning against Republican incumbent Sen. John Cornyn, appeared on stage and thanked the president. BY: MEGA The rally marked Trump’s third visit to Texas in less than a month as he urges voters to cast their ballots for Paxton, at a time when Republicans are pouring money into races they had expected to win comfortably in the midterms. Paxton, whom Trump endorsed after turning against Republican incumbent Sen. John Cornyn, appeared on stage and thanked the president. “Mr. President, I want to thank you for coming for me, for coming for us and for coming for Texas,” Paxton said. “We are going to win this race.”
Trump called Paxton “perhaps the greatest attorney general in the United States of America” and said, “He was tough and he was with us all the way. He’s a fantastic man.”
At a rally the previous week, Trump called Paxton a “pain in the a**.” However, he also said that he did not regret endorsing him over Cornyn, whom some pundits considered the safer choice.

summary: At least half a dozen protesters interrupted the president as he urged Texas voters to support Republican Senate candidate Ken Paxton, with some escorted away by police and one demonstrator reportedly assaulted while leaving the arena. At least one confrontation escalated beyond verbal exchanges and got physical, as an older Trump supporter assaulted a protester as the demonstrator attempted to leave the arena. “He was clearly stating U.S. cities would have been threatened if a nuclear Iran hadn’t been stopped,” White House communications director Steven Cheung said earlier this week.
